questions.question: Trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, this means:

options.text: The brakes are working properly.
The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes are new.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle pulls to one side while braking, you may have a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.

questions.question: The ____ shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.

options.text: Application pressure gauge
Air compressor governor
Supply pressure gauge
Drum brake

questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT part of an air brake system?

options.text: A service brake system
A parking brake system
An emergency brake system
An axle brake system

questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three separate braking systems: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about ____ to your total stopping distance.

options.text: 32 feet
15 feet
50 feet
10 feet

questions.explanation: Total stopping distance for air brake vehicles has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your stopping distance.

questions.question: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.
Should not come on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: When driving a double or triple, remember that:

options.text: It needs more space than most other vehicles.
Other drivers will get out of your way when needed.
It weighs about the same as other vehicles.
It can fit easily into small spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: It needs more space than most other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples need more space than other vehicles. They are longer and their size and weight prevent them from turning or stopping quickly. Always make sure you have enough space before entering traffic, crossing traffic, or changing lanes.

questions.question: When entering traffic with a double or triple, remember that these vehicles:

options.text: Need more space to merge than smaller vehicles.
Are exempt from most speed limits.
Are hard for other drivers to see.
Are not allowed on interstates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need more space to merge than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples need more space than other vehicles because they are longer and their size and weight prevent them from turning or stopping quickly. Always make sure you have enough space before entering traffic, crossing traffic, or changing lanes.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle is:

options.text: 10 psi in one minute
8 psi in one minute
6 psi in one minute
4 psi in one minute

questions.explanation: You need to know the maximum air loss rate for your vehicle. A triple combination should not lose more than 6 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: The air storage tanks:

options.text: Hold enough air for only one braking cycle.
Hold enough air for several braking cycles if the compressor fails.
Do not hold air unless there is an emergency.
Hold enough air for more than 1,000 braking cycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold enough air for several braking cycles if the compressor fails.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the air storage tanks hold enough air for the brakes to work several times if the compressor stops working.

questions.question: Is driving at night safe?

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. You cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare can hurt your vision. More tired and impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times. Press hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times. Press hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times. Press hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly upward.
Pump the brakes three times. Press hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times. Press hard on the brake pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: To test hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times. Then press hard and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak.

questions.question: What should you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
Honk your horn.
Wave to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians don't see you. Be ready in case they suddenly move into your path. You can lightly tap your horn or flash your lights as you pass.

questions.question: What is most likely to cause hydroplaning?

options.text: Using tires with worn tread
Using properly inflated tires
Using new tires
Traveling at speeds under 10 mph

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is most likely on wet roads if your tires are low on air or have worn tread. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What do anti-lock brakes do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking up
Lock up the front wheels
Keep a vehicle from speeding uphill
Keep a vehicle from speeding downhill

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking up
questions.explanation: Anti-lock brakes (ABS) prevent your vehicle's wheels from locking up when you brake hard.

questions.question: When driving, where should you look?

options.text: Keep your eyes in front of your vehicle.
Look in front and to the right.
Look in front and to the sides.
Look in front, to the sides, and behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look in front, to the sides, and behind.
questions.explanation: Safe driving means being aware of everything around your vehicle. Watch the road ahead and check your mirrors often. This helps you see what is beside and behind your vehicle.

questions.question: Why drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs to be replaced
Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
To allow air pressure to change
To remove bad air from the tanks

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that must be removed
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. If these build up in the system, they can damage the brakes. You must drain the tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and oil from the air tanks.
Stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
Activates emergency brakes when there is a leak.
Holds spring brakes in place until they are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve goes between the air compressor and the first tank. It prevents air from leaving the system if the compressor leaks.

questions.question: When should you shift gears based on road speed?

options.text: Learn what speed range each gear works best at and shift up as needed.
Watch other vehicles and try to match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as your guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speed range each gear works best at and shift up as needed.
questions.explanation: You should learn which speeds work best for each gear. Watch your speedometer and shift up when needed. Check your vehicle's manual for the right engine speeds to use for each gear.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up in an unfamiliar area?

options.text: Get out and walk around to see what is there.
Don't use both mirrors because it causes too much distraction.
Wait for someone else to back up first.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to see what is there.
questions.explanation: Backing up is always risky because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you don't know the area, get out and walk around first. This helps you see what you need to avoid before you back up.
